source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine - Engine Tune Up, p.6-6

procedures.title: Intake manifold: tighten
steps: Follow the sequence on the Torque Sequence Chart.

procedures.title: Fuel lines and fuel filter: service
steps: Check fuel lines for kinks, bends or leaks and fix any found.
Check the filter and replace it if plugged.
notes: For poor high-speed performance, run the fuel pump tests in Section 6M.

procedures.title: Cooling system: tune-up service
steps: Check for leaks, soft hoses, loose clamps and correct coolant level; service as needed.
notes: A pressure test (Additional Checks and Adjustments) can find internal or external leaks.

procedures.title: Accelerator linkage: check and adjust
steps: Disconnect the accelerator rod from the carburetor throttle lever.
Hold the throttle lever wide open.
Pull the accelerator rod to its wide open position (through the detent with automatic transmission).
Adjust the rod so it drops freely into the throttle lever hole.
Reconnect the rod at the throttle lever.
notes: Accelerator linkage details are in Section 6M.

procedures.title: Crankcase ventilation (closed positive): service
steps: Test the ventilation valve as described under Additional Checks and Adjustments.
Check hoses for deterioration or plugging.
If a flame arrestor is fitted, take it out, wash it in solvent and blow it dry with compressed air.
notes: All engines use the Closed Positive system: manifold vacuum pulls air from the carburetor air cleaner through the engine and a regulating valve into the manifold so fumes are burned; the oil filler cap is non-vented (see figure 10 in the manual).

procedures.title: Air injection reactor system: tune-up inspection
steps: Look for leaks, deteriorated hoses, cracked air manifolds or tubes and loose clamps.
Check the air pump belt condition and tension.
